title: Result of status.get (v1.0, first cut: the telemetry catalogue extends it)

heap.description: Internal RAM; null on a platform with no heap API.

min_free.description: Lowest free since boot; null where not tracked.

worker_stack_free.description: nRF52 only: the least free stack of the task that runs interface requests, once it has run.

psram_free.description: Absent on a board without PSRAM.

battery_mv.description: null when the board cannot measure it.

contacts.description: The contact list; absent on a role that has none (the Repeater and Room server).

connectivity.description: Absent on a build without connectivity modes.

ble_started.description: Companion: whether this boot's BLE stack came up. Absent when this boot did not start BLE.

lora.description: The LoRa link's counts since boot (LORA_MANAGEMENT.md section 7)

rf.description: Companion, once a reply frame has come, and never in an answer over LoRa (it would take a whole status past one signed reply): what became of replies to its rf.request since boot: replies (reply frames received), completed (messages they made), the lora counts for that side (LORA_MANAGEMENT.md section 7), and last_incomplete once a reply expired with frames missing

last_incomplete.description: The last reply that expired with frames missing: its xid, its frame count, and have, a mask of the frames that came (bit i: frame i).

lora_tx.description: Companion, once it has queued a LoRa management frame, and never in an answer over LoRa: what became of those frames since boot. A message's first frame is counted apart from the rest: queued, and sent (on air); then failed (the radio refused it), held (waited for airtime) and untracked (more in flight than the trace keeps).

events_dropped.description: Companion, once any: signed events dropped since boot because a link's queue had no room for them, all links together. Each one is a usig_seq gap on that link. Never in an answer over LoRa.

cable_dropped.description: Companion on nRF52, once any: frames dropped since boot because the USB host held the port open without reading for 20 ms. Never in an answer over LoRa.

inbox.description: What was received for the manager (OPERATIONS.md section 6.4): receptions this boot, those held and not acknowledged, and those lost.

messages.description: The message outcome table (OPERATIONS.md section 6): sends still open, and final outcomes not yet collected.

jobs.description: The job table (OPERATIONS.md section 3.2): the job open, and terminal results not yet acknowledged.

update.description: Present only while the image of an update job runs unconfirmed: that job, and the version and SHA-256 of the running image (UPDATES.md section 7, step 3), with unconfirmed:true when its job is already over.

sha256.description: null on the nRF52, whose bootloader installs a package the device cannot hash: the version is the attestation (UPDATES.md section 6).

unconfirmed.description: The job ended without a confirmation, yet this image runs: the image before it failed its trial each time it was sent back (UPDATES.md section 7, step 6).

deployment.description: Present only once the device holds a Deployment record (AUTHORITY.md section 4); absent on a standalone device. A record that cannot be read reports only state corrupt.

auth_rejections.description: Unsigned or unverifiable requests refused since boot (AUTHORITY.md section 9).

fallback.description: One copy of the record is damaged; the device runs on the other.

auth_rejections.description: Unsigned or unverifiable requests refused since boot (AUTHORITY.md section 9).
